sections.title: Before reading: study Chapter 3 in How to read. A name becomes an accusation.

segments.text: 寧持大書，安持小書。安有全葉，有半葉；二葉有「寧」字。寧視名，視帙。
寧：「主人也。」
segments.speaker: char-ning

segments.text: 人持帙，立。
人：「主人也。」
segments.speaker: char-visitor

segments.text: 寧出門，視帙。帙有字，無名。安持二葉出門，寧取半葉。

inference_aids.art_brief: Outside an open doorway. Ning has taken the half leaf from An and looks at visitor’s loose wrapper; visitor stands with that wrapper. An retains the whole leaf and small book. Ning’s large book remains with her; do not invent another holder. No proof of theft, no readable writing.

segments.text: 寧：「客，盜也。」
segments.speaker: char-ning

segments.text: 人視半葉，止。
家有主人。父出門，安見父。
父：「主人也。」
segments.speaker: char-father

segments.text: 父取小書，視半葉。寧視父，持半葉。父無帙，客有帙。
母出門，見客。寧持半葉，母取全葉。母視全葉，見「寧」字。
母：「客，盜也。」
segments.speaker: char-mother

segments.text: 客立，父閉門。安視門，止。
先生持卷，行。父見先生，開門。先生入門，父入門。母還全葉，安取全葉。寧持大書入門，客持帙入門。母入門，安入門。
先生視客，取帙。
寧：「客，盜也。」
segments.speaker: char-ning

segments.text: 先生：「使者也。」
segments.speaker: char-teacher

segments.text: 先生還帙，客取帙。客有帙，先生有卷。

exercises.title: Place the assertion at the end
exercises.instruction: Different miniature incidents, not claims about the story. Type the Chinese form selected by each cue: 1: An is a guest in a new incident; finish the assertion (yě); 2: the person is a father in a new incident; finish the assertion (yě); 3: the mother is a guest in a new incident; finish the assertion (yě); 4: the father is a teacher in a new incident; finish the assertion (yě); 5: this new guest is the owner of an object (zhǔrén). Story links point to prior forms or patterns, not to these new incidents.

obrazec.rule: In the assertion pattern practised here, put 也 (yě) at the end; no modern verb for ‘is’ is inserted.

exercises.title: Identify a role without changing the form
exercises.instruction: Different miniature incidents, not claims about the story. Type the Chinese form selected by each cue: 1: the person is a mother (mǔ); 2: Ning sees a father (fù); 3: the father sees a guest (kè); 4: Ning takes a fascicle (juàn); 5: the mother sees a messenger (shǐzhě). Story links point to prior forms or patterns, not to these new incidents.

obrazec.rule: In this new incident the person is a messenger. Use the whole taught role word.

sections.title: The teacher separates a role from an accusation

segments.text: 先生開卷。卷有字，有姓。父視姓，母視卷。卷有紙。先生取紙，安見紙。家有客，客立；父取大書，寧坐。

inference_aids.art_brief: Inside the house, teacher opens a fascicle and takes a separate loose sheet. Father has taken the large book from Ning and also has the small book. Ning sits holding the half leaf; An has the whole leaf. Mother watches; visitor retains loose wrapper. Do not depict a resolved book owner or extra sheets.

segments.text: 先生：「客，使者也。」
segments.speaker: char-teacher

segments.text: 客開帙，視帙。帙無紙。客閉帙，視紙。先生持紙，安視紙。
父還大書，寧取大書。父閉門。先生視父，視母。
先生：「父，主人也。母，主人也。安，子也。」
segments.speaker: char-teacher

inference_aids.gloss: 父｜主人｜也；母｜主人｜也；安｜子｜也

segments.text: 安立，母視安。
寧開大書，視破葉。先生視卷，視破葉。卷有姓，破葉無姓。大書有多字，紙有少字。父持小書，視紙。先生閉卷。
母取小書，父視卷。母開小書。安還全葉，母取全葉，視葉。寧持半葉，視名。二葉有名，名同。母持全葉，視子。
寧還大書，客取大書。客閉大書，持大書。
寧：「使者也。」
segments.speaker: char-ning

segments.text: 父視客，開門。
先生：「書有主人。客，使者也。」
segments.speaker: char-teacher

segments.text: 客出門，止。

exercises.title: Nominal assertions in different incidents
exercises.instruction: Different miniature incidents, not claims about the story. Type the Chinese form selected by each cue: 1: Ning is a child; finish the assertion (yě); 2: the teacher is a father; finish the assertion (yě); 3: the person is a guest; finish the assertion (yě); 4: this sheet is a whole leaf (quán yè); 5: this messenger is a guest (kè). Story links point to prior forms or patterns, not to these new incidents.

obrazec.rule: In this new incident, identify a detached whole leaf with a specific loose sheet of paper. Complete the assertion pattern.

exercises.title: Retrieve the stated object or action
exercises.instruction: Different miniature incidents, not claims about the story. Type the Chinese form selected by each cue: 1: the mother holds a fascicle (juàn); 2: An looks at a surname (xìng); 3: a child holds a whole leaf (quán yè); 4: a guest has a damaged leaf (pò yè); 5: a teacher gives back paper (huán). Story links point to prior forms or patterns, not to these new incidents.

obrazec.rule: Name the object, not its owner: a teacher holds paper.

sections.title: The paper bears An’s name; another paper is missing

segments.text: 先生持紙，安取紙。安視紙，見「安」字。紙有名，無姓。全葉有「寧」字；紙有「安」字。名異。安持紙，視母。

inference_aids.alt: Different names are found on the sheet and leaf.
inference_aids.art_brief: An holds the separate loose sheet and sees his name; mother holds the whole leaf bearing Ning’s name; teacher is nearby with the fascicle. Do not draw readable invented text; the prose identifies the actual written characters. Do not identify either sheet as the messenger’s missing note.

segments.text: 母：「子有紙。」
segments.speaker: char-mother

segments.text: 父取紙，視名。父還紙。安取紙。安視師，持紙。
先生開卷，父視姓。卷有姓，紙無姓。父視師，視姓。母還全葉，寧取全葉。寧持二葉，安持紙。
客視帙，開帙。帙無紙。客視大書，開書。大書有破葉，無紙。客閉大書，視門。
寧持全葉出門，安持紙出門。客視全葉，視紙。客視「安」字，安持紙。
客：「失紙。紙有字。」
segments.speaker: char-visitor

segments.text: 安視「安」字，止。
父出門，視客。家有主人，有客；母有書，客失紙。母閉小書，先生持卷。師視安，視寧，寧持二葉，安持紙。

exercises.title: Classify a role and track a possession
exercises.instruction: Different miniature incidents, not claims about the story. Type the Chinese form selected by each cue: 1: a guest is a father (fù); 2: a teacher is a mother (mǔ); 3: a sheet bears the same written character (tóng zì); 4: a child has no book wrapper (zhì); 5: a teacher takes a half leaf (bàn yè). Story links point to prior forms or patterns, not to these new incidents.

obrazec.rule: A different household has a teacher. Use the word naming that role.

exercises.title: Reading reference in new complete sentences
exercises.instruction: Different miniature incidents, not claims about the story. Type the Chinese form selected by each cue: 1: the mother has a whole leaf (yǒu); 2: a guest has no fascicle (wú); 3: a child opens a wrapper (kāi); 4: a teacher takes a small book (qǔ); 5: the mother closes a large book (bì). Story links point to prior forms or patterns, not to these new incidents.

obrazec.rule: The cue selects having (yǒu), not absence. Do not enter pinyin.

cover.art_brief: Undated fictional premodern doorway. Ning holds the large book and the half leaf; An holds the small book and whole leaf. Visitor holds a separate loose wrapper. Door open. Do not imply the visitor is a thief or show an established owner. No readable invented writing.

grammar.title: 客，使者也
grammar.rule: 客｜使者｜也。父｜主人｜也。安｜子｜也。

tables.caption: Read across: named subject, asserted role, final particle
An assertion about identity and a statement of possession do different work

grammar.note_en:
Study the four Chapter 3 packets in How to read before beginning this story. They introduce the new written roles and objects, including multi-character words. A compound is not permission to read each of its characters independently in every meaning. The popups select the meaning and modern Mandarin reading needed here. This is constructed literary narration, not a historical quotation.

A nominal predicate identifies or classifies a named subject using a noun expression. In 客，使者也, “the visitor is a messenger,” 客 identifies the person and 使者 gives the role being asserted. In the assertion pattern practised here, 也 yě comes at the end. It is a particle: a short grammatical word marking the assertion, rather than a thing or action. There is no English-style verb “is” between these two nouns. The comma separates the named subject for the novice reader; it does not add another word. The construction says what a person or thing is, rather than merely saying what it has.

Compare the earlier 客有帙, “the visitor has a wrapper,” with 客，使者也, “the visitor is a messenger.” 有 states possession. 也 does not replace 有: it follows the whole identifying assertion. The narrative also contrasts 父，主人也, “the father is the host,” and 安，子也, “An is a child.” Written nouns and particles stay the same for different subjects. No new endings or modern linking verb are required.

The assertions classify roles, while the surrounding actions change custody. 卷 juàn names the written volume or fascicle that the teacher carries, not the action of rolling something. 紙 zhǐ names the separate loose sheet removed from it. Here absence of 紙 in a wrapper or book means absence of a separate sheet, not that its ordinary leaves have no paper material. Do not combine the volume and sheet into one object in the custody ledger. A term naming an object and a statement identifying its owner are different kinds of claim.

Read an assertion together with its speaker. 寧：「客，盜也。」 is Ning saying “The visitor is a thief.” It is an accusation. It is not an independently established fact supplied by the narrator. 母：「客，盜也。」 repeats the accusation that the visitor is a thief, with her own speaker identified. 盜 dào is the role noun “thief” in these utterances; no verb meaning “steal” is required in this chapter’s answers. The teacher replies 使者也, “A messenger.” The teacher’s short 使者也 assertion describes the visitor explicitly named in the preceding accusation. A speaker label tells us who speaks, not necessarily who the assertion describes. A locally attributed short assertion can leave that directly discussed person understood. Keep its local referent; do not guess a new subject across paragraphs.

The wrapper dispute similarly contains two attributed 主人也 assertions, “The owner.” The contextual popup selects claimed owner there. In the household scene, 主人 identifies a host or householder, while 客 kè identifies the visitor. A messenger carries something for a purpose; identifying him as 使者 shǐzhě does not prove that he owns the book or wrapper, and a familiar written name does not prove ownership either. The visitor’s precise purpose and the ultimate owner remain open. Do not silently convert a character’s accusation or claim into a solved fact.

先生 xiānsheng is the respectful teacher title here; its last syllable is conventionally light in this citation reading. 師 shī also identifies the teacher. In 安視師，持紙, “An looks at the teacher while holding the sheet,” 師 refers to the same person previously called 先生. The new written word does not introduce a second teacher. 父 fù and 母 mǔ are An’s father and mother in this episode. 子 zǐ selects “child” in 安，子也 and the other references to An as a child. It is not a newly licensed polite word for “you.” 家 jiā selects the household, rather than the physical act of entering a building.

Surnames and names are different kinds of identifying information, but only their separate taught nouns are needed here: 姓 xìng is a surname or family name; 名 míng is a name. 卷有姓 means “the fascicle bears a surname”; 紙有名，無姓 means “the sheet has a name but no surname.” The surname on the fascicle is not printed out or identified in this reading, so An is not being asked to read untaught characters or establish a family connection. The sheet explicitly shows 安, while the whole leaf shows 寧. 名異, “the names differ,” summarizes that visible contrast. It does not establish the sheet’s author or owner.

At the end the messenger reports 失紙, “Lost the paper.” His following 紙有字, “the paper bears writing,” identifies a written sheet, or note. The preceding search shows that his wrapper and the large book do not contain it. An holds a sheet with his own written name; the prose does not establish that it is the messenger’s missing note. The new problem is which paper has gone missing, not a completed recovery. In open C, answer with a full event or attributed assertion supported by the reading. Do not use a bare role label where the task asks what happened.

A.title: Pensa A — Make an identifying assertion

obrazec.rule: Worked example: identify a specific loose sheet as a detached book leaf. Different incidents. In the assertion pattern practised here, put 也 at the end. No modern linking verb is being taught. Cues: 1: the teacher is a guest; complete the assertion; 2: this detached whole leaf is a loose sheet; complete the assertion; 3: the mother is a teacher; complete the assertion; 4: the person is a child; complete the assertion.

Supply the role or object identity named by the cue. The assertion keeps the same order. Cues: 1: a father is a messenger (shǐzhě); 2: a teacher is an object's owner (zhǔrén); 3: this detached leaf is a loose sheet (zhǐ); 4: a guest is a child (zǐ).

B.title: Pensa B — Retrieve the role or object; three bank entries are extra

obrazec.rule: Different miniature incidents. Supply exactly the named studied noun; no word changes are needed. 1: paper (zhǐ); 2: name (míng); 3: fascicle (juàn); 4: surname (xìng); 5: messenger (shǐzhě); 6: teacher (shī); 7: guest (kè); 8: owner (zhǔrén). The worked example asks for a teacher (shī).

C.title: Pensa C — Distinguish assertions from observed events
C.instruction: Continue each cue with a complete Chinese event sentence or an attributed assertion supported by the story. Do not turn a character’s accusation into narrator-confirmed truth. A name, yes/no or repetition of the cue is insufficient.

items.rubric: Retrieve Ning's ownership claim or accusation as attributed speech. A bare claim that the visitor actually is a thief is not a narrator-established fact; merely repeating that Ning looks at the wrapper does not answer.
Retrieve the father's closing of the door and/or An stopping at it; require a complete event sentence, not a role label.
Retrieve the teacher's identification of the visitor as a messenger. Equivalent full wording 客，使者也 is acceptable. Do not infer that the visitor owns either book.

model_answers: 客取大書，閉大書。客持大書出門。
items.rubric: Retrieve the messenger taking, closing or carrying the large book out. Do not treat the return as proof of ownership.

model_answers: 紙有「安」字，全葉有「寧」字。名異。
items.rubric: Require the differing written An and Ning names on the sheet and whole leaf. Saying only that they bear writing or names is insufficient; no unknown surname reading is required.

model_answers: 使者失紙。帙無紙，大書無紙。
items.rubric: Retrieve the messenger's missing paper/note and/or his unsuccessful search in wrapper or large book. The cue supplies An's possession, not the loss. Do not assert that An's sheet is certainly the messenger's missing note.

notes: Original constructed graded narration, not an authentic or adapted quotation. No audio or generated image.
Nominal assertions and source claims are distinguished. The visitor’s messenger role is identified by the teacher; neither this nor the Ning name proves book ownership.
All thirteen chapter2 sense IDs are semantically recalled; the final paper/note loss is the row’s assigned hook, not a new book/leaf-loss gag.
Father and mother are An’s parents; the new speaker IDs remain distinct. No actual unlearned surname is printed or guessed by An.
Full workbook30 and Pensa A8/B8/C6. Different-incident English cues select exact Chinese answers; open C remains meaningful story recall.

review_questions.question: LZH03-Q1: [?] Audit G03 nominal assertions and all inherited G01/G02 scope, especially attributed 主人也/盜也, compound lookup, role changes, and the distinction between reported accusation and narrator fact.

LZH03-Q2: [?] Check all object/door states and custody against chapter2. Does the visitor’s disputed wrapper and messenger identification lead coherently to Ning’s book return, An’s name-bearing sheet and the still-missing note? No owner, innocence or paper identity should be invented.

LZH03-Q3: [?] Assess first-use preparation including compounds and constructions, load and substantial varied reading/practice. Are the family roles meaningful to the scene rather than a vocabulary parade? Every new entry must recur three times meaningfully.

LZH03-Q4: [?] Adjudicate all closed variants and B alternatives under complete cues, all open C rubrics and source links, every grammar claim/table and pinyin/contextual sense. C6 must retrieve a missing-paper fact beyond its cue.
